correctness.rationale: For every real t with 0<t≤1 the oriented edge relation p1+p2+p3+t p4=0 identifies dual ball K_t=[−1,1]^3 intersect |u1+u2+u3|≤t. Extreme dual vertices are permutations of (1,−1,±t), with t=1 degeneracy handled. The eight signed edge molecules are exactly primal vertices because each edge is shorter than its alternative path. The algebraic identity (t,1,−1)=(1,t,−1)−(1−t)[(1,−1,t)+(1,−1,−t)]/2, with symmetries, bounds every nonnorming extreme dual evaluation by (2−t)v(T), norming ones by v(T), and p4 is always normed. Therefore ||T||≤(2−t)v(T). The rank-one map T=φ⊗z, φ(p_i)=(1,−1/2,−1/2), z=((1−t)/(1+t))p1+(2/(1+t))p2 has ||φ||=1, ||z||=2−t, v(T)=1 by vertex enumeration. The identities and witness arithmetic were checked symbolically and against the declared finite exact parameter verifier, but the proof treats the continuous interval, not only sampled rational t. Endpoint t=1 yields index 1; t→0 limit 1/2 is not a claimed degenerate four-point metric.
residual_risks: Real scalars only and equal-three-edge 0<t≤1 model; t=0 is not a positive four-vertex metric, arbitrary weights not handled.
